reviews.body: Welcome Erin! A couple of house rules inline, all quick.

comments.author: bob
comments.body: The handler opened a session and inserted the card directly. Here we keep handlers thin: they call one service function, and the service owns the session and the queries (ADR-003, and CONTRIBUTING's Layout section). Makes the logic reusable from the jobs too.

comments.author: erin
comments.body: Ah, at my last company we did it in the route, but I see the point. Moved into `saved_cards.save_card`.

comments.author: bob
comments.body: Creating a card isn't moving money, but it does call the tokenizer, and a double submit from checkout would create two cards. We decorate client-facing POSTs like this with `@idempotent` (ADR-004).

comments.author: carol
comments.body: This was `datetime.utcnow()`. We always use `app.utils.clock.now()`: it's tz-aware UTC and the `frozen_clock` fixture can control it in tests.

comments.author: erin
comments.body: Done, and I used frozen_clock in the test to assert on it.

comments.author: carol
comments.body: Test names follow `test_<unit>__<scenario>__<expected>` (see CONTRIBUTING), and please build the customer with `tests/factories.py` rather than constructing it inline.

comments.author: erin
comments.body: Renamed both and switched to make_customer.

comments.author: frank
comments.body: Add type hints to the test functions and fixtures (`fake_repos: FakeRepos`, `-> None`, etc.).

comments.author: erin
comments.body: Happy to. Is that the convention? The existing tests don't seem to have them.

comments.author: bob
comments.body: It isn't: we don't type tests, and mypy excludes tests/. Leave them as they are.
